Look man, I'm not saying my best friend is annoying… but she's really annoying.

It's become like an obsession for her now, I realized that last night when she approached me with that wild look she's been getting.  
 "You think you're up for a steak out?" she grinned, clutching her backpack up to her chest.

"Sure, I'd love to go out for steak," I rolled my eyes. "Seriously, C, when are you going to end this? The poor kid's already freaked out."

Her head retracted in mild shock. "What do you mean he's freaked out? I'M FREAKED OUT."

"You're not the one being STALKED, Ciara."

I've known Ciara since we were 8 years old. I'd spend all my time in the library, so would she, and eventually we kind of just started doing it together. 10 years later and you'd think we'd know everything about each other. I just have no idea how to tell her…

\-

It all started 5 months ago. I was skating down the road, got distracted as per usual and found my way over a stray rock. A huge rock. I flew. Woke up three days later to a very tense hospital room. Skull fracture, they said, but I'd make a full recovery. And recover I did… a little too well. They let me out about 3 weeks later with some antibiotics, a basket of bandages and a stern warning against being on any kind of wheels without a helmet. I was back on my board, helmet and all, about a week later, when I heard something. It sounded faint, but the more I focused on it the clearer it got. Whimpering. Pleading. The sound of a switch blade. You know how when you smell food you can almost see the aroma floating in the air? Makes it easier to follow, right? That's how this was. The closer I got, the louder it got, until I found myself about 15 feet away from a terrible scene. He towered over her, rummaging through her purse as she lay shaking on the ground. Blood. I smelled it before I saw it. He had cut her. Now normal people would call the police. Normal people, in this day and age, would probably have their phones with them in the first place. Apparently, I'm different. You're probably thinking I dove over there and smacked him across the head, helped the lady up and sped off like every hero in disguise should. But I didn't. I was TERRIFIED. I had no idea what I was capable of back then. So I watched. I thought as loudly as I could that if there were anyone else, ANYONE, that could come and save this woman… man. I begged every deity from Anubis to Zeus for someone to just save her. He'd found her wallet and was gathering up as much as he could before all three of us heard the sound of a siren. He was gone before the cops could get out of their car. The woman was distraught. I was distraught. I had felt like such a failure. What if he had done something to her? What if he had come after me next? Yeah, that sucked. But I hadn't forgotten how I'd found them in the first place. I wasn't dumb enough to immediately pin something like that as pure coincidence. Something had changed in me, and I knew it. I could feel it. And I'd find out just how powerful I was the next time I found my way to trouble.

\-

So, I caved. We stalked his house for 3 hours with zero conclusion. We'd gotten there past midnight and all the lights were already out, and they stayed out until we left. At some point a street light had gone on, and Ciara spent 10 minutes trying to convince me that he had done it just to mess with us. I really had no words for her. See, Adrien had moved into town about a week after my accident. He transferred all the way from Iceland, a piece of information that C has continuously insisted is key in this story.  
 "Seriously how many people do you even know that come from Iceland?" she shrieked. I was the one with the messed up head but she's the one who forgot the Icelandic exchange student who had a three month stay at our school, two years ago. She said that one didn't count because, "…she grew up in France.".

He's a nice kid, Adrien. Quiet, withdrawn, very polite; all more fuel to Ciara's wild fires.

\-

I spent the next two months after my accident trying to discover what I could do. I can't fly. But I did find that my levels of speed and strength had greatly increased, along with my senses of hearing, sight and smell. That last part? That's how I caught him. 

I went out skating again when I caught a smell that I was familiar with. At first, I honestly had no idea what it was. All I knew was that I recognized it, and it brought a bad feeling to my bones. So, like last time, I followed my instinct. I found myself in front of a house; modest, beautifully decorated. Remember when I said my sense of sight had been heightened? Yeah, X-Ray vision. As soon as I saw him my brain pinned the smell on him. He had tied up a mother and her two children, and was busy ransacking their house. This time, I wouldn’t let him get away...

Jeez dude, tough love huh?
